arguments: Macro (heavy weight): QQQ at $679.35 is below both its 50-day ($720.23) and 200-day ($681.17) averages. Only 22% of stocks are above their 50-day average, and tech (XLK) has lagged SPY by 10.6 points over 20 days. This is the main reason I hold back on swing entries.

Rates and credit (moderate support): the 10-year yield is down 0.36 points in 4 weeks to 4.86%, which eases pressure on high-valued tech. Credit spreads are steady, so there is no stress in lending. This argues the sell-off is about tech valuations, not a broader crisis.

Leadership (supporting evidence): health care (XLV +14.83), staples (XLP +12.35) and other non-tech sectors are leading SPY. Money is rotating rather than leaving stocks, which fits a sideways SPY and a falling QQQ.
